content.text: Curretly it is show the message "RDF was not parsable" to the client. What is the better message?
how about "There are syntax errors in the RDF file"?
Regards to internal logging, do you mean add a LOGGER.debug() ?
The solution to this ticket may be similar to:
, but likely requires digging into the code to find where the specific exception message is being nested inside of the more general MalformedRdfException.
RDF was not parsable: [line: 7, col: 29] Undefined prefix: ore
RDF was not parsable: [line: 5, col: 1 ] Unknown char: `(96;0x0060)
Yes, the messages you note would be more helpful for clients.
When creating a container resource with an RDF body, if the RDF is invalid in some way, it would be helpful if the message found in the internal logging would be sanitized and returned to the client.
Where "body.rdf" can be any of the attached "body.*.rdf" documents.

comments.body:
Curretly it is show the message "RDF was not parsable" to the client. What is the better message?
how about "There are syntax errors in the RDF file"?

Regards to internal logging, do you mean add a LOGGER.debug() ?

The solution to this ticket may be similar to: https://jira.duraspace.org/browse/FCREPO-1368 , but likely requires digging into the code to find where the specific exception message is being nested inside of the more general MalformedRdfException.

Will it be better?

RDF was not parsable: [line: 7, col: 29] Undefined prefix: ore

RDF was not parsable: [line: 5, col: 1 ] Unknown char: `(96;0x0060)
Yes, the messages you note would be more helpful for clients.
